Philip Ruddock, a former Liberal minister, has been appointed by the Australian cabinet to assess whether current laws sufficiently protect the human right to religious freedom. Announced on Wednesday, the review aims to head off a contentious debate surrounding proposed religious amendments to the same-sex marriage legislation. Treasurer Scott Morrison clarified, however, that the inquiry is “no substitute” for incorporating such amendments directly into the marriage bill.

***

Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull emphasized the need for careful examination of religious freedom issues following the “yes” vote on marriage equality and the upcoming legislative process. Significant internal division exists within the government regarding timing: senior conservatives including Peter Dutton and Mathias Cormann advocate for a separate religious freedom bill to be considered next year, while Morrison and Liberal Senator David Fawcett insist the matter must be addressed concurrently with marriage equality legislation.

***

Turnbull cautioned that numerous legislative proposals to protect religious freedom have emerged, many extending well beyond the specific context of marriage. He warned parliament to proceed with caution, citing the high risk of unintended consequences when legislating fundamental rights. The government is particularly wary of broadly worded, bill of rights-style declarations that could introduce legal uncertainty rather than clarity.

***

Describing the initiative as a “timely expert stocktake,” Turnbull stated that Ruddock’s findings would provide a measured foundation for any necessary legislative reforms. Ruddock has been directed to submit his report by 31 March, ensuring parliament can deliberate with informed precision rather than under political pressure.

***

Turnbull affirmed Ruddock’s suitability for the role, highlighting his prior service as Australia’s special envoy for human rights. This appointment underscores the government’s intent to address the complex intersection of religious freedom and marriage equality with expertise, neutrality, and deliberate care.
